# Purpose

This report summarizes validation and benchmark results generated by the training project. It reads `results/benchmark_results.csv`; it does not contain invented timing values. Render the main document first so the CSV is current.

# Environment

```{r}
cat(R.version.string, "\n")
cat("data.table:", as.character(packageVersion("data.table")), "\n")
cat("bench:", as.character(packageVersion("bench")), "\n")
```

# Dataset and output checks

The seeded generator creates 80 synthetic subject records and 320 synthetic laboratory records. The clinical transformation selects non-missing ALT and AST results, joins subject information, derives an age group, and writes `results/clinical_lab_summary.csv`.

```{r}
benchmark_file <- if (file.exists("../results/benchmark_results.csv")) {
  "../results/benchmark_results.csv"
} else {
  "results/benchmark_results.csv"
}
if (!file.exists(benchmark_file)) {
  stop("Run/render the main document first to create benchmark_results.csv.")
}
benchmark_results <- read.csv(benchmark_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
benchmark_results
```

# Measured performance

The median time is reported in seconds. Memory allocation is reported in bytes. Iterations per second is higher for faster repeated operations; garbage-collection rate is workload-dependent. Compare the methods within each task only. The benchmark uses 80,000 synthetic subjects and 320,000 lab records, with the subject table keyed before the timed join. Results describe this R/container setup and should not be treated as universal.

```{r}
stopifnot(nrow(benchmark_results) == 6L)
stopifnot(all(c("task", "implementation", "median_seconds", "memory_bytes",
                "iterations_per_second", "gc_per_second") %in%
              names(benchmark_results)))
benchmark_results[order(benchmark_results$task,
                       benchmark_results$implementation), ]
```

For a simple comparison, divide the base-R median and allocation by the data.table values. A ratio above 1 means the data.table result was lower for that measurement in this run. This ratio describes only the current measured setup.

```{r}
base_metrics <- benchmark_results[
  benchmark_results$implementation == "base R",
  c("task", "median_seconds", "memory_bytes")
]
dt_metrics <- benchmark_results[
  benchmark_results$implementation == "data.table",
  c("task", "median_seconds", "memory_bytes")
]
comparison <- merge(base_metrics, dt_metrics, by = "task",
                    suffixes = c("_base", "_data_table"))
comparison$speed_ratio <- comparison$median_seconds_base /
  comparison$median_seconds_data_table
comparison$memory_ratio <- comparison$memory_bytes_base /
  comparison$memory_bytes_data_table
comparison[order(comparison$task), ]
```

# Validation record

All equivalence checks run before timing in the main document. The six lesson scripts were executed against the supplied CSV files. The filter comparison and keyed join comparison passed; the end-to-end transformation produced a 12-row summary for the seeded inputs. Benchmark timings and memory numbers appear above only after a successful render.

# Limitations

The input data are small and synthetic. The benchmark expands them to provide a larger but still simple workload. Results depend on the machine, R and package versions, and background load. Key creation is excluded from the timed join because it is prepared once outside the benchmark. For a workflow that rebuilds keys for each operation, include that setup in its performance measurement.
